newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight ends at 8.0 pct after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight ends at 8.0 pct after choppy session.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended at 8.0 percent after trading as high as 9.0 percent following a warning by Bank Negara that it would take stern steps, including increasing interest rates, to stamp out speculation in the ringgit, dealers said.
Bank Negara governor Ahmad Mohamed Don said on Wednesday that due to current situation, the central bank had no choice but to allow interest rates to go up again.

"Otherwise we will only be inviting speculative activity in the ringgit if the rates are not allowed to rise given the shortage of ringgit in the market," he said in an interview with the national Bernama news agency.
Dealers said the overnight rate jumped after the news but it was pulled back down as overnight funds were still readily available. The overnight traded around 6.0 percent on Tuesday.
"It's settling around eight percent. At the moment, it's still very unclear what Negara is going to do," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
The governor's remarks also pushed swaps to the right, dealers said.
One-month swaps rose to 100 points from 65/70 before Ahmad's interview hit the market. Three-month swaps surged to 400/420 from 330/350.
Earlier, interbank rates across the board were at 8.0 percent against 7.7 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers said rates were likely to stay firm on Thursday due to an expected outflow of funds resulting from Bank Negara's intervention in the foreign exchange market.
The central bank was said to have sold an estimated $1 billion on Tuesday to help the ringgit.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell sharply across the board as players liquidated positions in anticipation on rising interbank rates.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down 17 points to 92.32, or an implied yield of 7.68 percent.
The December contract fell 13 to 92.52, or 7.48 percent and March 1998 was down 10 to 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
